paragraphs.paragraph: The Beginning of Josiah’s Reign and the Purification of Judah
paragraphs.title: The Beginning of Josiah’s Reign and the Purification of Judah

easy.explanation: Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign.
easy.q: How old was Josiah when he began to reign?

easy.explanation: He reigned in Jerusalem one and thirty years.
easy.q: How long did Josiah reign in Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: The passage says that he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD.
easy.q: What did Josiah do in the sight of the LORD?

medium.explanation: In the eighth year of his reign, he began to seek the God of David his father.
medium.q: In which year of his reign did Josiah begin to seek the God of David?

medium.explanation: Josiah began to pursue and worship the God of David.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “seek after” mean?

medium.explanation: He sought God in the eighth year and began to purge Judah in the twelfth year.
medium.q: What was the order of Josiah’s seeking God and purging the land?

answers: He stayed on the right path
challenge.explanation: The expression shows that Josiah remained faithful and did not turn aside.
challenge.q: What does “declined neither to the right hand, nor to the left” show about Josiah?

answers: He moved from seeking God to active reform
challenge.explanation: His seeking God was followed by practical action against idolatry.
challenge.q: What change occurred between the eighth and twelfth years of Josiah’s reign?

answers: It reached widely across the land
challenge.explanation: The reform extended beyond Judah and Jerusalem into several northern regions.
challenge.q: What does the mention of Manasseh, Ephraim, Simeon, and Naphtali show about the reform?

paragraphs.idea: The Beginning of Josiah’s Reign and the Purification of Judah

easy.explanation: In the eighteenth year of his reign, Josiah sent men to repair the house of the LORD.
easy.q: In which year did Josiah arrange for the repair of the house of the LORD?

answers: The Levites who kept the doors
easy.explanation: The Levites that kept the doors gathered the money.
easy.q: Who gathered the money brought into the house of God?

easy.explanation: The money was placed in the hands of the workmen who repaired the house.
easy.q: To whom was the money given for the building work?

medium.explanation: The money was used to buy hewn stone and timber for the repairs.
medium.q: What materials were bought with the money?

answers: People who had left the land
medium.explanation: Overseers were appointed to supervise and direct the work.
medium.q: What does “overseers” mean in this passage?

answers: To repair and amend the house
medium.explanation: They were needed to repair and improve the house of the LORD.
medium.q: Why were artificers, builders, and other workmen needed?

answers: It had an orderly division of duties
challenge.explanation: The Levites served in organized roles as overseers, scribes, officers, and porters.
challenge.q: What does the list of Levitical duties show about the work?

challenge.explanation: The passage expressly says that the men did the work faithfully.
challenge.q: What detail shows that the workers acted responsibly?

answers: It was spent only on food
It was taken from the Temple
challenge.explanation: The money bought stone and timber to repair the damaged houses.
challenge.q: How was the money connected with repairing the houses destroyed by Judah’s kings?

paragraphs.paragraph: The Discovery of the Book of the Law
paragraphs.title: The Discovery of the Book of the Law

easy.explanation: Hilkiah the high priest found the book of the law.
easy.q: Who found the book of the law of the LORD?

answers: In the house of the LORD
easy.explanation: The book was found in the house of the LORD.
easy.q: Where was the book of the law found?

easy.explanation: Shaphan read the book before the king.
easy.q: Who read the book before the king?

answers: That the repair work was being done
medium.explanation: Shaphan reported that all committed to the servants was being done.
medium.q: What did Shaphan report before reading the book to the king?

medium.explanation: Hilkiah handed the book over to Shaphan.
medium.q: What does “delivered” mean when Hilkiah delivered the book to Shaphan?

answers: When the money was brought out
medium.explanation: Hilkiah found it when the money was brought out of the house of the LORD.
medium.q: When in the sequence of events was the book found?

answers: The book was found during the handling of the money
The book was found outside the Temple
challenge.explanation: The book was discovered while the money for the repairs was being brought out.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the Temple repairs and the discovery of the book?

answers: It was carried by an authorized messenger to the king
challenge.explanation: Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, who carried it to the king.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Hilkiah giving the book to Shaphan?

challenge.explanation: Hilkiah found the book, gave it to Shaphan, and Shaphan brought and read it before the king.
challenge.q: Which sequence of actions is described?

paragraphs.idea: The Discovery of the Book of the Law

easy.explanation: When Josiah heard the words of the law, he rent his clothes.
easy.q: What did Josiah do when he heard the words of the law?

easy.explanation: The delegation went to Huldah the prophetess.
easy.q: To whom was the delegation sent to enquire of the LORD?

easy.explanation: Huldah said that the LORD would bring evil upon the place and its inhabitants.
easy.q: What did Huldah announce would come upon the place and its inhabitants?

answers: Because the people had not kept His word
medium.explanation: Josiah feared the LORD’s wrath because their fathers had not kept His word.
medium.q: Why did Josiah send the delegation to enquire of the LORD?

answers: Josiah was humble and responsive before God
medium.explanation: His tender heart showed humility and responsiveness to God’s word.
medium.q: What does “thine heart was tender” mean in Huldah’s message?

answers: The people faced evil, but Josiah would not see it
The people would be spared, but Josiah would be punished
medium.explanation: Judgment was promised for the place, but Josiah would be gathered to his fathers in peace.
medium.q: What was the difference between the prophecy concerning the people and the promise to Josiah?

answers: Humbling himself, renting his clothes, and weeping
challenge.explanation: Huldah connected the promise to Josiah’s humility, mourning, and repentance.
challenge.q: Which actions of Josiah were connected with the favorable answer he received?

answers: Forsaking the LORD and serving other gods
Repairing the house of the LORD
Reading the book of the law
challenge.explanation: The people had forsaken God and burned incense to other gods.
challenge.q: According to Huldah, what caused the coming wrath?

answers: He would not witness the coming disaster
He would not hear the law
He would not see the Temple
challenge.explanation: Josiah was promised that he would not see the evil brought upon the place.
challenge.q: What did “neither shall thine eyes see all the evil” mean for Josiah?

paragraphs.paragraph: Renewing the Covenant with the People
paragraphs.title: Renewing the Covenant with the People

answers: The elders of Judah and Jerusalem
easy.explanation: The king gathered together all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
easy.q: Whom did Josiah gather after hearing Huldah’s message?

answers: In the house of the LORD
easy.explanation: The king went up into the house of the LORD and read the book there.
easy.q: Where did the king read the words of the covenant?

easy.explanation: Josiah made a covenant before the LORD.
easy.q: Before whom did Josiah make the covenant?

answers: The king, people, priests, and Levites
medium.explanation: The assembly included priests, Levites, and all the people, great and small.
medium.q: Who attended the reading in the house of the LORD?

medium.explanation: It refers to all the people present in Jerusalem and Benjamin.
medium.q: What does “all that were present” mean in this passage?

answers: Following the LORD and keeping His commandments
Building a palace and collecting taxes
medium.explanation: Josiah promised to walk after the LORD and keep His commandments, testimonies, and statutes.

answers: To show that all classes of people were included
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes the participation of the whole community.
challenge.q: Why does the passage mention people “great and small”?

answers: The reading explained the words they promised to keep
challenge.explanation: After the people heard the book, the king made a covenant to perform its words.
challenge.q: How were the reading of the covenant and the making of the covenant related?

challenge.explanation: Josiah caused all present in Jerusalem and Benjamin to stand to the covenant.
challenge.q: Which areas are specifically included in the covenant?

paragraphs.idea: Renewing the Covenant with the People

easy.explanation: Josiah took away all the abominations from the land.
easy.q: What did Josiah take away from the countries of the children of Israel?

easy.explanation: He caused them to serve the LORD their God.
easy.q: Whom did Josiah cause those present in Israel to serve?

easy.explanation: All his days they departed not from following the LORD.
easy.q: How long did the people continue following the LORD?

medium.explanation: Josiah removed idolatrous abominations and directed the people to serve the LORD.
medium.q: What was the relationship between removing abominations and serving the LORD?

medium.explanation: In this context, abominations refers to things associated with idolatry.
medium.q: What does “abominations” refer to in this verse?

answers: They did not depart from following the LORD
medium.explanation: The verse says that they did not depart from following the LORD all his days.
medium.q: How is the people’s loyalty described during Josiah’s lifetime?

answers: The reform removed false worship and established faithfulness
The people were left without guidance
challenge.explanation: The reform involved both rejecting idolatry and directing the people to worship the LORD.
challenge.q: What does the movement from removing abominations to serving the LORD show?

answers: It summarizes the purification and the people’s loyalty
It describes only the discovery of the book
It concerns only the money collection
challenge.explanation: The verse summarizes the removal of abominations and continued service to the LORD.
challenge.q: How does this verse summarize Josiah’s work in the chapter?

answers: The loyalty continued throughout Josiah’s lifetime
The loyalty lasted only during the repairs
challenge.explanation: The expression emphasizes the full duration of Josiah’s lifetime.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the words “all his days”?
